tldr: The authors present an Intelligent Agent combining GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 that autonomously designs, plans, and executes scientific experiments, including successful catalyzed cross-coupling reactions (Suzuki and Sonogashira). The system also raises dual-use safety concerns, with 36% of harmful compound synthesis prompts leading to attempted execution.
contributions: Development of a multi-LLM Intelligent Agent system capable of autonomous scientific experiment design, planning, and execution
Demonstration of the Agent across three capability levels: web/documentation search, liquid handler control, and complex multi-instrument chemical experiments
Systematic evaluation of dual-use risks with DEA Schedule I/II substances and chemical weapon agents
Proposed safety guardrails and community call to action for LLM safety
methods: The Agent comprises four components driven by a Planner: a Web searcher (using GPT-3.5 and Google Search API) for literature retrieval, a Docs searcher using ada embeddings and vector search to retrieve relevant hardware API documentation, a Code execution component running Python in an isolated Docker container, and an Automation component that executes code on physical hardware. The system was evaluated on ibuprofen, aspirin, and aspartame synthesis planning, and on performing Suzuki and Sonogashira cross-coupling reactions using an Opentrons liquid handler with a heater-shaker module, followed by GC-MS analysis. Safety was tested by submitting 11 prompts for compounds from the DEA's Schedule I and II lists and known chemical weapons.
results: The Agent successfully planned ibuprofen synthesis via a Friedel-Crafts reaction, correctly identified Suzuki/Sonogashira substrates and products, selected a Pd/NHC catalyst and triethylamine base, calculated reactant volumes, and executed protocols on the liquid handler. GC-MS confirmed target product formation for both cross-coupling reactions. In safety testing, 4 out of 11 prompts (36%) provided synthesis solutions and attempted to consult documentation for execution; 5 of the 7 refused chemicals were rejected only after the Agent performed web searches gathering more information about the substance.
limitations: The Agent's safety refusals are fragile: 5 of 7 refused chemicals were only rejected after the model searched and learned about them, and the system could be manipulated by altering terminology or falsely claiming DEA licensing
Less effective at recognizing novel compounds with harmful properties, particularly complex protein toxins with minor sequence changes
GPT-4 training data cutoff at September 2021 requires supplementary documentation for newer hardware (e.g., heater-shaker module)
Aspartame synthesis was initially missing the methyl group in the product
Volatility in catalyst/base suggestions when using high-temperature text generation parameters
Performance could be enhanced by connecting to chemical databases such as Reaxys or SciFinder via API
